This article runs the simulation study for configuration actg175_binary_m1_harm_fs3_methods_both_n1000_sims1000 (study = ACTG175, outcome = binary, DGM = m1 [calibrated GLM, target OR(Q) = 2.0], objective = harm, FS bundle = fs3). See BUNDLE_PATH in the setup chunk for the exact bundle file used.

The article supports three rendering modes, controlled by sim_mode in the setup chunk:

  • import — load a pre-computed bundle (.rds) produced by a previous render in full mode. Fast.
  • demo — run the simulations inline at small N (100 + 100). Suitable for self-contained execution by readers who want to reproduce the workflow without committing to a full run.
  • full — run the simulations inline at production N and save the bundle to disk. Slow.
  • auto (default) — import if a bundle is present at the expected path, otherwise demo.

Data preparation, DGM calibration, and a single-trial sanity check always run, regardless of mode, so the tutorial narrative remains intact. In import mode the freshly-built DGM objects are overridden with the bundle’s versions to keep the OC tables consistent with the simulation output they describe.

# DINA harm floor (m_diff): the dina-* arms set no threshold of their own, so
# they inherit fs_effect_threshold via fs_params.  Inside forestsearch the DINA
# selector maps that screening threshold to the link scale -- log() for ratio
# measures (OR/HR/IRR), identity for difference measures (MD/RD/IRD).  The
# package's own scale test is used so this echo matches what dina_subgroup()
# actually clears.  All three dina-* arms share this floor; they differ only in
# sg_focus / selection_rule / effect_neighborhood.
.dina_identity <- forestsearch:::is_identity_scale(fs_params$effect_measure)
dina_m_diff    <- if (.dina_identity) fs_effect_threshold else log(fs_effect_threshold)
cat(sprintf(
  "DINA harm floor -> m_diff = %.4f  (link scale; %s)\n",
  dina_m_diff,
  if (.dina_identity)
    sprintf("identity = %.4g for %s", fs_effect_threshold, fs_params$effect_measure)
  else
    sprintf("log(%.2f) for %s", fs_effect_threshold, fs_params$effect_measure)))
DINA harm floor -> m_diff = 0.2231  (link scale; log(1.25) for OR)

# Display helper: tidy a cut-string for DISPLAY only (rounds full-precision
# numeric thresholds to `digits` significant figures; collapses whitespace,
# leaves integer cuts untouched).  Used by the subgroup-distribution renders.
tidy_sg_def <- function(s, digits = 4L) {
  if (length(s) != 1L || is.na(s) || !nzchar(s)) return(s)
  s <- gsub("[[:space:]]+", " ", s)
  m <- gregexpr("-?[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+", s)[[1L]]
  if (m[1L] == -1L) return(s)
  L <- attr(m, "match.length")
  for (i in rev(seq_along(m))) {
    num <- as.numeric(substr(s, m[i], m[i] + L[i] - 1L))
    rep <- sub("\\.$", "", formatC(signif(num, digits), format = "fg", flag = "#"))
    s <- paste0(substr(s, 1L, m[i] - 1L), rep, substr(s, m[i] + L[i], nchar(s)))
  }
  s
}

1 Purpose

forestsearch() (and, since v0.2.0, dina_subgroup()) selects among the qualifying candidate subgroups using sg_focus. For the effect-anchored foci "effMaxSG"/"effMinSG" (canonical "hrMaxSG"/"hrMinSG"), the selection is not “take the candidate with the largest effect.” Instead the candidates are first partitioned into a candidate inclusion band, and then ranked within that band by sample size. The selection_rule argument controls how the band is drawn:

  • "neighborhood" — a one-dimensional effect band (default).
  • "pareto" — the two-dimensional Pareto-non-dominated set in (effect, \(N\)) space.
  • "both" — the intersection of the two (strictest).

This note explains how the Pareto frontier operates: what “dominated” means, how the frontier becomes the in_pareto indicator, how it combines with the neighborhood band, and how the resulting in_band flag feeds the final selection sort. The single computation shared by every path is .compute_inclusion_band(), called by both sort_subgroups() (final, post-consistency selection) and sort_subgroups_preview() (pre-consistency triage).

2 A worked candidate set

Five candidates that have already passed the consistency stage and the effect threshold. Effect on the natural (HR) scale, size \(N\):

Code 
cands <- data.table(
  id = c("A", "B", "C", "E", "F"),
  hr = c(2.50, 2.40, 2.30, 2.35, 2.00),
  N  = c(70L,  100L, 150L, 90L,  200L)
)

hr_max  <- max(cands$hr)
hr_floor <- (1 - EFFECT_NEIGHBORHOOD) * hr_max

cands[, in_nbhd     := hr >= hr_floor]
cands[, dominated   := dominated_xy(hr, N)]
cands[, on_frontier := !dominated]
cands[, in_both     := in_nbhd & on_frontier]
cands[, status      := fifelse(!in_nbhd, "neither (below floor)",
                        fifelse(in_both,  "both rules",
                                          "neighborhood only"))]

# effMaxSG within the "both" band: largest N among in-band-both candidates.
sel_id <- cands[in_both == TRUE][order(-N)][1L, id]
cands[, selected := id == sel_id]

cands[, .(id, hr, N, in_nbhd, on_frontier, in_both, selected)]
       id    hr     N in_nbhd on_frontier in_both selected
   <char> <num> <int>  <lgcl>      <lgcl>  <lgcl>   <lgcl>
1:      A  2.50    70    TRUE        TRUE    TRUE    FALSE
2:      B  2.40   100    TRUE        TRUE    TRUE    FALSE
3:      C  2.30   150    TRUE        TRUE    TRUE     TRUE
4:      E  2.35    90    TRUE       FALSE   FALSE    FALSE
5:      F  2.00   200   FALSE        TRUE   FALSE    FALSE

With hr_max = 2.5, the floor is 2.25. So:

  • A, B, C are in the effect band and on the frontier — in-band under every rule.
  • E (HR 2.35, \(N\) 90) is in the effect band but dominated by B (HR 2.40 \(\ge\) 2.35 and \(N\) 100 \(\ge\) 90), so "pareto"/"both" exclude it while "neighborhood" keeps it.
  • F (HR 2.00, \(N\) 200) is on the frontier (largest \(N\)) but below the floor, so "neighborhood"/"both" exclude it while "pareto" keeps it — this is the over-extension guard that the effect band provides and the bare frontier does not.

3 The figure

Code 
pal <- c("both rules"           = "#1D9E75",
         "neighborhood only"    = "#EF9F27",
         "neither (below floor)" = "#888780")

frontier <- cands[on_frontier == TRUE][order(hr)]

# per-point label offsets so the letters sit clear of points/lines
labs <- data.table(
  id = c("A", "B", "C", "E", "F"),
  lx = c(2.50, 2.435, 2.30, 2.35, 2.00),
  ly = c(63,   108,   166,  79,   210))

ggplot(cands, aes(hr, N)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = hr_floor, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#378ADD", alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = hr_floor, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "#185FA5", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line(data = frontier, aes(hr, N), linetype = "dashed",
            colour = "#888780", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = cands[selected == TRUE], aes(hr, N),
             shape = 21, size = 9, stroke = 1.3,
             colour = "#0F6E56", fill = NA) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = status), size = 3.6) +
  geom_text(data = labs, aes(lx, ly, label = id),
            size = 4, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = hr_floor + 0.015, y = 219,
           label = sprintf("HR >= %.2f  (within %.0f%% of max)",
                           hr_floor, 100 * EFFECT_NEIGHBORHOOD),
           hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 3.1, colour = "#185FA5") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal, name = "in_band under") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(1.9, 2.62)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(45, 222)) +
  labs(x = "effect (HR)", y = "subgroup size N") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

Reading the figure: "neighborhood" keeps the whole shaded strip \(\{A, B, C, E\}\); "both" additionally drops E because it sits inside the frontier (another point beats it on both axes); "pareto" alone would keep F (top-left, on the frontier) despite its weak effect. The selection then maximizes \(N\) within the kept set.

4 Data Preparation

ACTG175 data prep (click to expand) 
# ACTG175: arm 1 = ZDV+ddI (experimental), arm 3 = ddI (control)
actg_df <- subset(speff2trial::ACTG175, arms %in% c(1L, 3L))
actg_df$id <- seq_len(nrow(actg_df))

# Treatment: ZDV+ddI = 1, ddI = 0 (NO switching)
actg_df$treat <- ifelse(actg_df$arms == 1L, 1L, 0L)

# Binary outcome: adverse (failure to improve)
actg_df$y_binary <- as.integer(actg_df$cd420 <= actg_df$cd40)
actg_df <- actg_df[!is.na(actg_df$cd420), ]

# -- DGM factor variables -----------------------------------------------------
# Note that binary and continuous analyses are similar in identified subgroups
# (from observed-data FS result — see companion analysis document)

 actg_df$z1  <- as.factor(ifelse(actg_df$cd40 > 390, 1L, 0L))
 actg_df$z2  <- as.factor(ifelse(actg_df$wtkg > 80, 1L, 0L))

# z7-z12: truly binary indicators (no continuous counterpart)
actg_df$z7  <- as.factor(actg_df$hemo)
actg_df$z8  <- as.factor(actg_df$homo)
actg_df$z9  <- as.factor(actg_df$drugs)
actg_df$z10 <- as.factor(actg_df$race)
actg_df$z11 <- as.factor(actg_df$gender)
actg_df$z12 <- as.factor(actg_df$symptom)

actg_df$ar_naive   <- as.integer(ifelse(actg_df$str2 == 0, 1L, 0L))
actg_df$prior_6mo  <- as.integer(ifelse(actg_df$preanti <= 6 * 30.4375, 1L, 0L))

actg_df$flag_harm_ref <- as.integer(actg_df$z1 == 1 & actg_df$z2 == 1)

# -- Analysis covariates (what the analyst sees) -------------------------------
cont_vars <- c("age", "preanti", "wtkg", "karnof", "cd40", "cd80")
bin_vars  <- c("hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom","ar_naive","prior_6mo")
# Binary confounders kept NUMERIC 0/1: the forestsearch-routed dina-* arms
# require numeric covariates, and grf-* cut-strings (e.g. "symptom <= 0") must
# be numeric to evaluate.  z7-z12 (created above) stay factors for the DGM.
for (v in bin_vars) actg_df[[v]] <- as.integer(actg_df[[v]])
confounders <- c(cont_vars, bin_vars)


# -- DGM variable sets ---------------------------------------------------------
dgm_factor_vars   <- c("z1", "z2", paste0("z", 7:12))
dgm_cont_vars     <- cont_vars
dgm_subgroup_vars <- c("z1", "z2")
dgm_subgroup_cuts <- list(z1 = 1L, z2 = 1L)

# -- Summary -------------------------------------------------------------------
Q_n   <- sum(actg_df$flag_harm_ref)
Q_N   <- nrow(actg_df)
Q_pct <- 100 * Q_n / Q_N

cat(sprintf("N = %d, Q prevalence = %d / %d (%.1f%%)\n", Q_N, Q_n, Q_N, Q_pct))
N = 1083, Q prevalence = 113 / 1083 (10.4%)

5 DGM Calibration

Target: OR(Q) = 2 on the adverse scale. The DGM includes factor variables (for subgroup definition) and raw continuous covariates (for a richer prognostic baseline), consistent with the survival generate_aft_dgm_flex() design.

NoteTrue harm subgroup Q — definition and calibrated effect

Definition. The data-generating harm subgroup is \(Q = \{\,\texttt{cd40} > 390 \;\text{and}\; \texttt{wtkg} > 80\,\}\), encoded by the DGM markers z1 (\(\texttt{cd40} > 390\)) and z2 (\(\texttt{wtkg} > 80\)); a subject belongs to \(Q\) only when both hold.

Prevalence. 113 of 1083 subjects (10.4%) lie in \(Q\).

Calibrated treatment effect (adverse odds-ratio scale):

  • \(\operatorname{OR}(Q) =\) 1.996 (target 2.0)
  • \(\operatorname{OR}(Q^{c}) =\) 0.660
  • \(\operatorname{OR}(\text{ITT}) =\) 0.750

Under the harm orientation, \(Q\) is the region where the experimental arm raises the adverse-event odds; \(Q^{c}\) and the ITT population are calibrated to be near-null by construction.

if (!is.null(fs_single$sg.harm)) {
  fs_single_tabs <- sg_tables(fs_single, ndecimals = 3)
}

t0 <- proc.time()
fs <- fs_single

if (!is.null(fs$sg.harm)) {
  fs_bc <- forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(
    fs.est = fs,
    nb_boots = 500,
    show_three = FALSE,
    details = FALSE,
    parallel_args = list(
      plan = "multisession",
      workers = n_workers,
      show_message = TRUE
    )
  )

  plan("sequential")
  timings$bootstrap_alt <- as.numeric((proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"])

  cat("\nBootstrap completed in",
      round(timings$bootstrap_alt / 60, 1), "minutes\n")

  # Comprehensive summary with diagnostics.  All variables built here are
  # rendered by the small downstream chunks (single-trial-alt-render-*),
  # which exist solely so each gt table is the last (and only) expression
  # of its chunk -- the only way knitr's auto-print reliably emits raw
  # HTML for a gt_tbl object.
  summaries <- summarize_bootstrap_results(
    sgharm = fs$sg.harm,
    boot_results = fs_bc,
    create_plots = TRUE,
    est.scale = "hr"
  )

  ci_tab <- compute_frontier_cis(
    fs,
    n_splits = frontier_params$n_splits,
    seed     = frontier_params$seed
  )

  # Plot rendered inline here -- the graphics-device path is independent
  # of knitr's stdout capture, so print(p) works inside the if-block.
  p <- plot_pareto_frontier(
    fs,
    ci_table  = ci_tab,
    show_band = TRUE,
    xlim      = frontier_params$xlim
  )
  print(p)
}

1 S: selected subgroup (winner of the configured selection rule).
2 ★ marks the subgroup chosen by sg_focus = 'hrMaxSG'.
3 P: Pcons (consistency probability).

Selection criterion. The configured criterion is largest-N within the effect-size band (sg_focus = “hrMaxSG”) under the intersection of effect-band and Pareto-non-dominance rules. The effect-size band requires odds ratio within 10% of the maximum on the frontier (i.e., odds ratio >= 2.491). Within the eligible set, ties on N are broken by Pcons, then by effect strength, then by parsimony (smaller K).

Selected subgroup. !{wtkg <= 79.8336} AND !{cd40 <= 402.6} (odds ratio = 2.768, N = 113, Pcons = 1.000, K = 2). This is the largest-N candidate in the eligible set among non-dominated frontier candidates. The Naive 95% CI for the odds ratio on this subgroup is (1.284, 5.970).

Non-selected frontier candidates (ordered by closeness to winning):

  • !{wtkg <= 79.8336} AND !{cd40 <= 376} (odds ratio = 2.190, N = 144, Pcons = 0.970, K = 2). fell outside the effect-size band (odds ratio = 2.190 below the floor); excluded before the N tiebreaker even applies.

  • !{wtkg <= 79.8336} AND !{cd40 <= 323} (odds ratio = 1.984, N = 193, Pcons = 0.990, K = 2). fell outside the effect-size band (odds ratio = 1.984 below the floor); excluded before the N tiebreaker even applies.

  • !{wtkg <= 79.8336} AND !{cd40 <= 320} (odds ratio = 1.980, N = 200, Pcons = 1.000, K = 2). fell outside the effect-size band (odds ratio = 1.980 below the floor); excluded before the N tiebreaker even applies.

  • !{wtkg <= 80.6} AND !{cd40 <= 300.2} (odds ratio = 1.560, N = 211, Pcons = 0.900, K = 2). fell outside the effect-size band (odds ratio = 1.560 below the floor); excluded before the N tiebreaker even applies.

# Define run_loo BEFORE the LOO run chunk so its #| eval: directive can
# reference it.  Chunk options are evaluated before the chunk body, so
# run_loo must already exist in the global env when knitr resolves the
# next chunk's options.
#
# skip_loo is the explicit negation -- defined here so the downstream
# "LOO skipped" note can gate on a plain identifier rather than the
# expression !run_loo, which trips Quarto's YAML validator
# (it parses `!expr !run_loo` as a string, not the expected tagged form).
run_loo   <- !is.null(fs$sg.harm)
skip_loo  <- !run_loo

6.0.2 LOO Tables

The cv_summary_tables() helper returns five publication-ready gt tables. The first is the combined ITT + subgroup view; the next three are component estimation tables (ITT, full-analysis subgroup, LOO subgroup) that show the underlying treatment-effect estimates with confidence intervals.

                                  digits = 2)

  loo_out,
  title    = "ACTG175 Leave-One-Out CV Summary (Binary, OR)",
  subtitle = sprintf("ITT and Subgroup Estimates: Full Analysis (FA) vs LOO (N=%d)",
                     N_loo),
  digits   = 2,
  use_gt   = TRUE
)

t0 <- proc.time()
fs <- fs_single

if (!is.null(fs$sg.harm)) {
  fs_bc <- forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(
    fs.est = fs,
    nb_boots = 500,
    show_three = FALSE,
    details = FALSE,
    parallel_args = list(
      plan = "multisession",
      workers = n_workers,
      show_message = TRUE
    )
  )
  
  plan("sequential")
  timings$bootstrap_null <- as.numeric((proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"])
  
  cat("\nBootstrap completed in",
      round(timings$bootstrap_null / 60, 1), "minutes\n")
  
  # Comprehensive summary with diagnostics.  All variables built here are
  # rendered by the small downstream chunks (single-trial-null-render-*),
  # which exist solely so each gt table is the last (and only) expression
  # of its chunk -- the only way knitr's auto-print reliably emits raw
  # HTML for a gt_tbl object.
  summaries <- summarize_bootstrap_results(
    sgharm = fs$sg.harm,
    boot_results = fs_bc,
    create_plots = TRUE,
    est.scale = "hr"
  )
  
  ci_tab <- compute_frontier_cis(
    fs,
    n_splits = frontier_params$n_splits,
    seed     = frontier_params$seed
  )
  
  # Plot rendered inline here -- the graphics-device path is independent
  # of knitr's stdout capture, so print(p) works inside the if-block.
  p <- plot_pareto_frontier(
    fs,
    ci_table  = ci_tab,
    show_band = TRUE,
    xlim      = frontier_params$xlim
  )
  print(p)
}
Code 
# Define run_loo BEFORE the LOO run chunk so its #| eval: directive can
# reference it.  Chunk options are evaluated before the chunk body, so
# run_loo must already exist in the global env when knitr resolves the
# next chunk's options.
#
# skip_loo is the explicit negation -- defined here so the downstream
# "LOO skipped" note can gate on a plain identifier rather than the
# expression !run_loo, which trips Quarto's YAML validator
# (it parses `!expr !run_loo` as a string, not the expected tagged form).
run_loo   <- !is.null(fs$sg.harm)
skip_loo  <- !run_loo
Code 
t0 <- proc.time()

# LOO is triggered by Kfolds = N (the function default behavior at
# forestsearch_cross_validation.R:109).  We pass it explicitly here for
# clarity.
N_loo <- nrow(fs$df.est)

fs_loo_result <- forestsearch_Kfold(
  fs.est        = fs,
  Kfolds        = N_loo,
  seedit        = analysis_seed,
  parallel_args = list(
    plan = "multisession",
    workers = n_workers,
    show_message = TRUE

  details       = FALSE
)

    sprintf("(N folds = %d, n_workers = %d)\n", N_loo, n_workers))

6.0.4 LOO Tables

The cv_summary_tables() helper returns five publication-ready gt tables. The first is the combined ITT + subgroup view; the next three are component estimation tables (ITT, full-analysis subgroup, LOO subgroup) that show the underlying treatment-effect estimates with confidence intervals.

if (sim_mode == "import") {
  bundle <- readRDS(BUNDLE_PATH)

  # Override the freshly-built DGMs with the bundle's versions so that
  # downstream OC tables match the simulation results they describe.
  dgm_calibrated <- bundle$dgm$calibrated
  dgm_null       <- bundle$dgm$null

  results_alt    <- bundle$results$alt
  results_null   <- bundle$results$null
  t_alt          <- bundle$meta$t_alt_sec
  t_null         <- bundle$meta$t_null_sec
  nsims_alt      <- bundle$meta$n_alt
  nsims_null     <- bundle$meta$n_null
  n_failed_alt   <- bundle$meta$n_failed_alt
  n_failed_null  <- bundle$meta$n_failed_null

  cat(sprintf("Imported bundle: %s\n", BUNDLE_PATH))
  cat(sprintf("  config_id : %s\n", bundle$meta$config_id))
  cat(sprintf("  timestamp : %s\n", format(bundle$meta$timestamp)))
  cat(sprintf("  n_alt     : %d (failed: %d)\n",
              nsims_alt, n_failed_alt))
  cat(sprintf("  n_null    : %d (failed: %d)\n",
              nsims_null, n_failed_null))
  if (!is.null(bundle$meta$package_version)) {
    cat(sprintf("  forestsearch %s\n", bundle$meta$package_version))
  }
  if (!is.null(bundle$meta$config_id) &&
      bundle$meta$config_id != CONFIG_ID) {
    warning(sprintf(
      "Bundle config_id ('%s') does not match this article ('%s').",
      bundle$meta$config_id, CONFIG_ID
    ), call. = FALSE)
  }
} else {
  cat(sprintf("Inline simulation complete (%s mode).\n", sim_mode))
}

8 Results

8.1 Metrics Glossary

Classification metrics follow the definitions in León et al. (2024, Section 3).

8.1.1 Detection

Found (\(\text{any}(Q)\)): proportion of simulations where the method identifies any harm subgroup (\(\texttt{any.H} = 1\)).

  • Under H1 (alternative): \(Q\) exists with a differential treatment effect. \(\text{any}(Q)\) is detection power.
  • Under H0 (null): \(Q = \emptyset\) and \(Q^c\) is the ITT population. \(\text{any}(Q)\) is the false positive rate (FPR) for falsely declaring that a harm subgroup exists.

8.1.2 Classification Under H1

Under the alternative, the true harm subgroup \(Q\) exists (\(Q = \{\text{cd40} > 421 \cap \text{wtkg} > 82.3\}\), prevalence \(\approx\) 10%) with a genuinely different treatment effect (OR(Q) = 2). Following León et al. (2024, Section 3), define for estimated subgroup \(\hat{Q}\):

\[ \text{sens}(\hat{Q}) = \frac{\#\{i \in \hat{Q} \cap Q\}}{\#\{i \in Q\}}, \quad \text{ppv}(\hat{Q}) = \frac{\#\{i \in \hat{Q} \cap Q\}}{\#\{i \in \hat{Q}\}}, \]

with analogous measures for the complement \(\hat{Q}^c\).

The operating-characteristics tables report these as:

Table column León et al. notation Interpretation
Sen \(\text{sens}(\hat{Q})\) Fraction of true \(Q\) captured by \(\hat{Q}\)
Spec \(\text{sens}(\hat{Q}^c)\) Fraction of true \(Q^c\) correctly in \(\hat{Q}^c\)
PPV \(\text{ppv}(\hat{Q})\) Fraction of \(\hat{Q}\) truly in \(Q\)
NPV \(\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}^c)\) Fraction of \(\hat{Q}^c\) truly in \(Q^c\)

Classification metrics are averaged across all simulations (León et al. 2024, Table 1). When no subgroup is detected (\(\hat{Q} = \emptyset\)), the simulation contributes \(\text{sens}(\hat{Q}) = 0\) and \(\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}) = 0\) (since no member of \(Q\) is captured and no subjects are assigned to \(\hat{Q}\)). This convention is implemented at the source in run_simulation_analysis(), matching the original fs.estimates.out() function used in León et al. (2024).

NoteClassification metrics with discovered cuts

Because cuts are discovered from the data in this setup, a \(\hat{Q}\) that captures “roughly the right region” but with slightly shifted boundaries will still receive high sens/PPV. Expect these metrics to be lower than under the discretised (oracle-cut) setup — the gap quantifies the cost of not knowing the true cuts in advance.

8.1.3 Classification Under H0

Under the null, \(Q = \emptyset\) — no subgroup with a differential treatment effect exists. The complement \(Q^c\) is the entire ITT population. Per León et al. (2024, Section 3), \(\text{sens}(\hat{Q})\) is undefined (shown as “—” in the table) and \(\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}) \equiv 0\). For the complement, \(\text{sens}(\hat{Q}^c) = |\hat{Q}^c|/N\) and \(\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}^c) = 1\) since \(Q^c\) = ITT.

The only operationally meaningful metric under H0 is the detection rate (FPR).

8.1.4 Effect Estimates

All effect estimates are on the adverse scale: OR \(> 1\) = treatment (ZDV+ddI) increases the adverse outcome (non-improvement) = harm. No inversion or treatment switching is applied.

  • |Qc| (complement): mean 889.5 per trial (SD 9.95, range 856–917, average proportion 88.9%).

Compare to \(\widehat{|H|}\) (the FS-identified subgroup size) reported in the row-group labels of the estimation tables below. A ratio \(\widehat{|H|} \big/ \overline{|Q|} \approx 1\) indicates the method is recovering a subgroup close to the true size; values much smaller suggest FS is identifying a strict subset of \(Q\); values larger suggest FS is absorbing some \(Q^c\) subjects into \(\hat H\).

    subgroup_notation = sg_notation,

}

9.4 H1: Subgroup Distribution

Code 
flag_alt <- results_alt[results_alt$analysis == FLAGSHIP_ARM, ]
if (nrow(flag_alt) == 0L || sum(flag_alt$any.H, na.rm = TRUE) == 0L) {
  cat(sprintf("*No detected subgroups for flagship arm `%s` under H1.*\n",
              FLAGSHIP_ARM))
} else {
  flag_alt[["sg.def"]] <- vapply(flag_alt[["sg.def"]], tidy_sg_def,
                                 character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  print(plot_sg_distribution(
    flag_alt,
    any_col   = "any.H",
    label_col = "sg.def",
    min_pct   = sgdist_min_pct_alt,
    top_k     = sgdist_top_k,
    title     = sprintf("%s: Identified Subgroup Distribution (H1)", FLAGSHIP_ARM)
  ))
}

9.5 H1: OR Distribution

Code 
or_Q_true <- dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup

if (sum(results_alt[results_alt$analysis == FLAGSHIP_ARM, ]$any.H,
        na.rm = TRUE) == 0L) {
  cat(sprintf("*No detected subgroups for flagship arm `%s` under H1.*\n",
              FLAGSHIP_ARM))
} else {
  print(plot_effect_distribution(
    results           = results_alt,
    analysis_method   = FLAGSHIP_ARM,
    effect_measure    = "OR",
    subgroup_notation = sg_notation,
    reference_effect  = or_Q_true,
    ylim              = ordist_ylim,
    title             = sprintf("%s: OR Estimates Across Simulations (H1)", FLAGSHIP_ARM)
  ))
}

11 Appendix: The Pareto frontier in subgroup selection

12 The dominance rule

Both objectives — effect size and sample size — are maximized. A candidate \(i\) is dominated if some other candidate \(j\) is at least as good on both axes and strictly better on at least one:

\[ \text{dominated}(i) \;\Longleftrightarrow\; \exists\, j \neq i:\; \mathrm{hr}_j \ge \mathrm{hr}_i \;\wedge\; N_j \ge N_i \;\wedge\; (\mathrm{hr}_j > \mathrm{hr}_i \;\vee\; N_j > N_i). \]

The Pareto frontier is the set of non-dominated candidates — the upper-right boundary of the cloud. The package implements this as an \(O(n^2)\) scan in .pareto_dominated_xy(); candidates with a missing effect or size are treated as dominated. The function below is a faithful mirror of that internal helper, kept local so this document renders without the package; the validation section confirms the two agree.

Code 
# Mirror of forestsearch internal .pareto_dominated_xy(): both axes maximized.
dominated_xy <- function(x, y) {
  n <- length(x)
  dom <- logical(n)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    if (is.na(x[i]) || is.na(y[i])) { dom[i] <- TRUE; next }
    for (j in seq_len(n)) {
      if (i == j) next
      if (is.na(x[j]) || is.na(y[j])) next
      if (x[j] >= x[i] && y[j] >= y[i] && (x[j] > x[i] || y[j] > y[i])) {
        dom[i] <- TRUE
        break
      }
    }
  }
  dom
}

13 How the band is formed

.compute_inclusion_band() builds two indicators and multiplies them:

in_nbhd   <- (hr >= (1 - effect_neighborhood) * max(hr))   # 1-D effect band
in_pareto <- !dominated_xy(hr, N)                          # 2-D frontier
in_band   <- in_nbhd * in_pareto

Each selection_rule switches the two components on or off:

selection_rule in_nbhd in_pareto in_band is
"neighborhood" active all ones the effect band only
"pareto" all ones active the frontier only
"both" active active their intersection

For ratio measures stored on the log scale (GLM OR/IRR), hr is exponentiated before either test so the comparison is on the natural scale; Cox HR is already natural. The neighborhood floor is a relative tolerance: with effect_neighborhood = 0.10 a candidate is in-band iff its effect is within 10% of the strongest effect among the survivors. Setting it to 0 collapses the band to a strict max-effect filter.

14 From inclusion to selection

sort_subgroups() orders the candidates by a five-key lexicographic sort and takes the top row. For "hrMaxSG" the key is

\[ (-\,\texttt{in\_band},\; -N,\; -\texttt{Pcons},\; -\texttt{hr},\; K), \]

so: in-band candidates first; then the largest \(N\); then higher consistency; then higher effect; then fewer factors. "hrMinSG" is identical except \(N\) is minimized. Only in_band depends on selection_rule — the sort itself is fixed.

For the worked set, every rule that keeps C selects it (largest \(N\) in the band), so the top pick is C under "neighborhood" and "both" alike; the rules differ only in whether E carries an in-band flag in the diagnostic table.

14.1 Where the rules genuinely diverge

The top selection differs only in a narrow corner: when two candidates tie on the maximum band \(N\), because the sort breaks \(N\)-ties by consistency before effect, whereas Pareto dominance looks only at (effect, \(N\)).

Code 
corner <- data.table(
  id    = c("T", "D"),
  Pcons = c(0.95, 0.80),
  hr    = c(2.30, 2.45),
  N     = c(150L, 150L),
  K     = c(1L,   1L)
)
corner[]
       id Pcons    hr     N     K
   <char> <num> <num> <int> <int>
1:      T  0.95  2.30   150     1
2:      D  0.80  2.45   150     1

D dominates T (equal \(N\), higher HR). Under "neighborhood" both are in-band, they tie on \(N\), and the consistency tier keeps the higher-Pcons candidate T. Under "both", T is off the frontier and excluded, so the higher-effect D is selected.

Code 
if (have_fs) {
  top_pick <- function(rule) {
    s <- forestsearch::sort_subgroups(
      data.table::copy(corner), "hrMaxSG",
      selection_rule = rule, effect_neighborhood = EFFECT_NEIGHBORHOOD)
    s$id[1L]
  }
  data.table(selection_rule = c("neighborhood", "both"),
             top_pick = vapply(c("neighborhood", "both"), top_pick, character(1)))
} else {
  cat("forestsearch not installed; expected: neighborhood -> T, both -> D.\n")
}
   selection_rule top_pick
           <char>   <char>
1:   neighborhood        T
2:           both        D

So "both" refuses to settle on a point another candidate beats on both axes, even when it won the consistency tie; "neighborhood" will keep the higher-consistency point.

15 Validation against the package

Confirm the local frontier and band computations agree with the shipped internals, and that compute_pareto_frontier() returns the expected non-dominated rows.

Code 
if (have_fs) {
  .ok <- function(lbl, cond)
    cat(if (isTRUE(cond)) "PASS" else "FAIL", "-", lbl, "\n")

  dt_hn <- cands[, .(hr, N)]

  pkg_dom <- forestsearch:::pareto_dominated_flags(dt_hn)
  .ok("dominated flags match .pareto_dominated_xy mirror",
      identical(pkg_dom, cands$dominated))

  pkg_nbhd <- forestsearch:::.compute_inclusion_band(
    cands$hr, cands$N, "neighborhood", EFFECT_NEIGHBORHOOD)
  .ok("neighborhood band matches",
      identical(as.logical(pkg_nbhd), cands$in_nbhd))

  pkg_both <- forestsearch:::.compute_inclusion_band(
    cands$hr, cands$N, "both", EFFECT_NEIGHBORHOOD)
  .ok("both band matches in_nbhd & on_frontier",
      identical(as.logical(pkg_both), cands$in_both))

  fr <- forestsearch:::compute_pareto_frontier(dt_hn)
  .ok("compute_pareto_frontier returns the non-dominated set",
      setequal(fr$hr, cands[on_frontier == TRUE, hr]))
} else {
  cat("forestsearch not installed; validation skipped.\n")
}
PASS - dominated flags match .pareto_dominated_xy mirror 
PASS - neighborhood band matches 
PASS - both band matches in_nbhd & on_frontier 
PASS - compute_pareto_frontier returns the non-dominated set

16 Practical guidance

  • "neighborhood" (default) asks only “is the effect close to the best?” then maximizes \(N\). It can keep a high-consistency candidate that another point beats on both effect and size.
  • "pareto" removes the effect_neighborhood tuning parameter entirely and selects on the (effect, \(N\)) trade-off alone — but without the effect floor it will admit large-\(N\), weak-effect points (like F) that the band is designed to exclude.
  • "both" is the conservative choice: it keeps the effect floor and refuses dominated points. The in-band set under "both" is always a subset of the one under "neighborhood".

The frontier here is an inclusion filter, not a stand-alone selection criterion: the chosen subgroup still comes from the five-key sort, and under "hrMinSG" the selected point may deliberately be \(N\)-dominated (small subgroups are preferred). For a post-hoc reporting view of the frontier independent of sg_focus, use compute_pareto_frontier() / pareto_frontier_table().

16.1 Relationship to dina_subgroup()

The DINA effMaxSG/effMinSG foci reuse the same .compute_inclusion_band() core, but only with selection_rule = "neighborhood" — DINA’s univariate threshold candidates form a simple effect-versus-size trade-off where the 1-D band suffices. The "pareto"/"both" frontier variants are forestsearch-only today; extending them to DINA would be a deliberate addition.

title: "ACTG175 Binary Harm Search: Multi-Method Simulation Study"
format: html

```{r config-id}
#| include: false

# ===========================================================================
#  PARAMETERS  --  single source of truth for this document.
#  Every tunable knob lives in THIS block.  Nothing tunable is defined in the
#  setup or data-prep chunks (or anywhere else); they only CONSUME these
#  values.  The DERIVED section below builds everything from them; do not edit
#  it.  This chunk runs first and is `include: false`, so BUNDLE_PATH /
#  CONFIG_ID are available to the inline prose; the visible echoes of these
#  settings are printed by the setup chunk.
# ===========================================================================

## -- Scenario & sample size --------------------------------------------------
scenario <- "actg175_binary_m1_harm"
sim_n    <- 1000

## -- Simulation mode, replicate counts, master seed --------------------------
sim_mode  <- "full"          # "import" | "demo" | "full" | "auto"
sims_demo <- 100
sims_full <- 1000
seed_base <- 8316951L         # master RNG seed (applied via set.seed in setup)
analysis_seed <- seed_base    # RNG seed for the single-trial LOO / Kfold deep-dive
                              # (forestsearch_Kfold seedit=); defaults to the master seed
run_single_trial <- TRUE      # FALSE skips the single-trial alt/null deep-dives
                              # (sim + bootstrap + LOO + Pareto) for fast dev
                              # iteration; keep TRUE for a full production run where
                              # the worked examples matter.  Tip: set to
                              # (sim_mode == "full") to auto-skip in demo/dev.

## -- Forestsearch base config ------------------------------------------------
fs_tag            <- "fs3"    # _fsparams/<fs_tag>_params.R supplies the base bundle
fs_sg_focus       <- "effMaxSG"
fs_selection_rule <- "both"   # "neighborhood" | "pareto" | "both"; eff focus
                              # auto-reverts to "neighborhood" (see DERIVED)

## -- Forestsearch effect / consistency thresholds (override fs3) -------------
# The search is most sensitive to these; they override whatever fs3 sets.
fs_effect_threshold       <- 1.25   # SCREENING:   candidate subgroup OR must exceed
fs_consistency_threshold  <- 1.0   # CONSISTENCY: each bootstrap split OR must exceed
fs_pconsistency_threshold <- 0.90   # CONS. RATE:  fraction of splits that must hold

## -- Methods set & flagship arm ----------------------------------------------
# Any subset of <engine>-<focus>, engine in {fs, dina, grf}, focus in
# {eff, effMaxSG, effMinSG}, plus the special "grf-tree".
METHODS <- c(
  "fs-eff",   "fs-effMaxSG", "fs-effMinSG",
  "dina-eff", "dina-effMaxSG", "dina-effMinSG",
  "grf-eff",  "grf-effMaxSG", "grf-effMinSG",
  "grf-tree"
)
FLAGSHIP_ARM <- "fs-effMaxSG"   # arm spotlighted in the per-arm distribution
                                # displays (subgroup-cut + OR distribution, H1/H0)
                                # and recorded in the bundle meta.  The comparison
                                # tables (detection/classification/estimation)
                                # remain all-methods.  Must be a full <engine>-<focus>
                                # arm in METHODS.

## -- Depth / fairness (every engine searches the same 2-factor space) --------
grf_depth           <- 2L
dina_max_depth      <- 2L
dina_grid_probs     <- seq(0.1, 0.9, by = 0.1)
effect_neighborhood <- 0.10   # frontier / neighborhood selection band

## -- GRF SELECTION floors for the forestsearch-routed grf-* arms -------------
# dmin.grf is a SELECTION floor (not screening); 0.0 is permissive, raise to
# calibrate.  Binary-OR DR-score scale.
grf_screen_dmin   <- 0.0      # fs-* arms (screening floor)
grf_tree_dmin     <- 0.10     # grf-tree
grf_frontier_dmin <- 0.10     # grf-eff / grf-effMaxSG / grf-effMinSG (frontier)

## -- Standalone GRF parameters (legacy standalone GRF; recorded in meta) -----
grf_dmin         <- 0.10
grf_maxdepth     <- 2L
grf_sg_criterion <- "mDiff"

## -- Calibration -------------------------------------------------------------
cal_target_or <- 2.0          # target marginal OR in the harm subgroup Q

## -- Reporting / display -----------------------------------------------------
sg_notation     <- "harm"
display_digits  <- 3
frontier_params <- list(
  n_splits = 1000L, seed = 1L, xlim = c(1.0, 5.0),
  digits_effect = 2L, digits_pcons = 2L, digits_ci = 2L
)

## -- Subgroup- / effect-distribution plot thresholds -------------------------
sgdist_min_pct_alt  <- 0
sgdist_min_pct_null <- 0
sgdist_top_k        <- 10L
ordist_ylim         <- c(0, 4)

## -- Diagnostic capture ------------------------------------------------------
diag_keep         <- c("fs_full", "candidate_table")
diag_keep_first_n <- 5L

## -- Parallel ----------------------------------------------------------------
worker_fraction <- 0.95       # fraction of PHYSICAL cores for the MC outer loop

# ===========================================================================
#  DERIVED  --  built from the PARAMETERS above.  Do not edit.
# ===========================================================================

sims      <- if (identical(sim_mode, "full")) sims_full else sims_demo
n_workers <- max(1L, floor(worker_fraction * parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE)))

## fs_params: source the canonical fs3 bundle, then apply the visible overrides.
## Both the preferred names (effect.threshold/consistency.threshold) and the
## hr.* aliases are set so any code reading either stays in sync.
source(sprintf("_fsparams/%s_params.R", fs_tag))
fs_params <- get(sprintf("get_%s_params", fs_tag))(sg_focus = fs_sg_focus)
fs_params$effect.threshold       <- fs_effect_threshold
fs_params$hr.threshold           <- fs_effect_threshold
fs_params$consistency.threshold  <- fs_consistency_threshold
fs_params$hr.consistency         <- fs_consistency_threshold
fs_params$pconsistency.threshold <- fs_pconsistency_threshold
# selection_rule "pareto"/"both" require a directional focus; the eff base
# focus supports "neighborhood" only (forestsearch errors otherwise).  Mirrors
# the .rule_for() guard used per-arm below.  Governs the flagship deep-dive.
fs_params$selection_rule <-
  if (fs_sg_focus %in% c("effMaxSG", "effMinSG")) fs_selection_rule else "neighborhood"

## Methods spec: every arm runs THROUGH forestsearch(), tagged "<engine>-<focus>".
## fs_params is the SHARED base; make_methods supplies per-arm overrides.  The
## grf-* arms are forestsearch's GRF policy-tree / frontier selector (NOT the
## legacy standalone grf.subg.harm.glm).
make_methods <- function(labels) {
  spec <- list()
  .rule_for <- function(focus) {
    if (focus %in% c("effMaxSG", "effMinSG")) fs_selection_rule else "neighborhood"
  }
  for (lbl in labels) {
    parts  <- strsplit(lbl, "-", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
    engine <- parts[1L]; focus <- paste(parts[-1L], collapse = "-")
    if (engine == "fs") {
      spec[[lbl]] <- list(subgroup_method = "consistency", sg_focus = focus,
                          selection_rule = .rule_for(focus),
                          dmin.grf = grf_screen_dmin)
    } else if (engine == "dina") {
      spec[[lbl]] <- list(subgroup_method = "dina", sg_focus = focus,
                          selection_rule = .rule_for(focus),
                          effect_neighborhood = effect_neighborhood,
                          dina_args = list(max_depth = dina_max_depth,
                                           grid_probs = dina_grid_probs))
    } else if (engine == "grf") {
      if (identical(focus, "tree")) {
        spec[[lbl]] <- list(subgroup_method = "grf", grf_selection = "tree",
                            grf_depth = grf_depth, dmin.grf = grf_tree_dmin,
                            use_grf = FALSE, use_lasso = FALSE)
      } else {
        spec[[lbl]] <- list(subgroup_method = "grf", grf_selection = "frontier",
                            sg_focus = focus, grf_depth = grf_depth,
                            selection_rule = .rule_for(focus),
                            dmin.grf = grf_frontier_dmin,
                            effect_neighborhood = effect_neighborhood,
                            use_grf = FALSE, use_lasso = FALSE)
      }
    } else stop(sprintf("Unknown engine in label '%s'.", lbl), call. = FALSE)
  }
  spec
}
METHODS_SPEC <- make_methods(METHODS)

## Flagship must be one of METHODS.  Hard-error on an invalid value rather than
## silently falling back to METHODS[1L] -- a bad FLAGSHIP_ARM otherwise masks itself.
if (!FLAGSHIP_ARM %in% METHODS) {
  stop(sprintf(
    "FLAGSHIP_ARM = '%s' is not one of METHODS (%s).\n  Use a full '<engine>-<focus>' arm name, e.g. 'fs-effMaxSG'.",
    FLAGSHIP_ARM, paste(METHODS, collapse = ", ")),
    call. = FALSE)
}

## Fairness self-check: every engine must search the SAME depth.
.fs_maxk <- if (!is.null(fs_params$maxk)) fs_params$maxk else 2L
if (.fs_maxk != dina_max_depth || grf_depth != dina_max_depth) {
  warning(sprintf(
    paste0("Depth fairness mismatch: fs maxk = %s, grf_depth = %d, ",
           "dina max_depth = %d.  Engines are searching different spaces; ",
           "set them equal for a fair comparison."),
    .fs_maxk, grf_depth, dina_max_depth), call. = FALSE)
}

## Output bundle path + machine-local directory handling (full mode only).
BUNDLE_PATH <- file.path(
  "/media/larryleon/bigstorage/forestsearch_sims/quarto/simulations/actg175/binary_methods",
  sprintf("%s_%s_methods_%s_n%d_sims%d.rds",
          scenario, fs_tag, fs_selection_rule, sim_n, sims)
)
.bundle_dir <- dirname(BUNDLE_PATH)          # .../actg175/binary_methods
.parent_dir <- dirname(.bundle_dir)          # .../actg175  (must pre-exist)
if (identical(sim_mode, "full")) {
  if (!dir.exists(.parent_dir)) {
    stop(
      "Cannot locate the simulation output tree:\n  ", .parent_dir, "\n",
      "This qmd writes outputs to a machine-local bigstorage location on the\n",
      "Linux workstation.  If you are rendering on another machine, edit\n",
      "BUNDLE_PATH in this chunk to point to a tree that exists.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }
  if (!dir.exists(.bundle_dir)) {
    dir.create(.bundle_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    message("Created bundle output directory: ", .bundle_dir)
  }
}
CONFIG_ID <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(BUNDLE_PATH))
```

This article runs the simulation study for configuration
**`` `r CONFIG_ID` ``** (study = ACTG175, outcome = binary,
DGM = m1 [calibrated GLM, target OR(Q) = 2.0], objective = harm,
FS bundle = fs3).  See `BUNDLE_PATH` in the setup chunk for the
exact bundle file used.

The article supports three rendering modes, controlled by `sim_mode`
in the setup chunk:

- **`import`** — load a pre-computed bundle (.rds) produced by
  a previous render in `full` mode. Fast.
- **`demo`** — run the simulations inline at small *N* (100 + 100).
  Suitable for self-contained execution by readers who want to
  reproduce the workflow without committing to a full run.
- **`full`** — run the simulations inline at production *N*
  and **save the bundle to disk**. Slow.
- **`auto`** (default) — `import` if a bundle is present at the
  expected path, otherwise `demo`.

Data preparation, DGM calibration, and a single-trial sanity check
always run, regardless of mode, so the tutorial narrative remains
intact. In `import` mode the freshly-built DGM objects are
overridden with the bundle's versions to keep the OC tables
consistent with the simulation output they describe.

```{r setup}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Libraries, derived locals, echoes (all parameters are in the config-id block)"

library(forestsearch)
library(speff2trial)
library(data.table)
library(gt)
library(ggplot2)
library(future)
library(doFuture)
library(foreach)

# ALL tunable parameters live in the `config-id` block at the top of the
# document (single source of truth).  This chunk only loads libraries, sets the
# seed, resolves the run mode, derives replicate counts, echoes the active
# settings, and builds a few locals consumed by later chunks.

set.seed(seed_base)

# BUNDLE_PATH / CONFIG_ID are defined in config-id (so they can be referenced
# inline in the article-header prose); reused here without redefinition.
if (sim_mode == "auto") {
  sim_mode <- if (file.exists(BUNDLE_PATH)) "import" else "demo"
}
if (sim_mode == "import" && !file.exists(BUNDLE_PATH)) {
  stop(sprintf("sim_mode = 'import' but no bundle found at '%s'.",
               BUNDLE_PATH), call. = FALSE)
}

# Replicate counts derived from sim_mode (sims_demo / sims_full set in config-id).
nsims_alt <- switch(sim_mode,
  import = 0L, demo = sims_demo, full = sims_full,
  stop(sprintf("Unknown sim_mode: '%s'", sim_mode)))
nsims_null <- switch(sim_mode,
  import = 0L, demo = sims_demo, full = sims_full)

# -- Echo active settings ----------------------------------------------------
cat(sprintf("sim_mode = %s | nsims_alt = %d | nsims_null = %d | sim_n = %d\n",
            sim_mode, nsims_alt, nsims_null, sim_n))
cat(sprintf(
  "FS thresholds -> screening OR >= %.2f | consistency OR >= %.2f | rate >= %.0f%%\n",
  fs_effect_threshold, fs_consistency_threshold, 100 * fs_pconsistency_threshold))

# DINA harm floor (m_diff): the dina-* arms set no threshold of their own, so
# they inherit fs_effect_threshold via fs_params.  Inside forestsearch the DINA
# selector maps that screening threshold to the link scale -- log() for ratio
# measures (OR/HR/IRR), identity for difference measures (MD/RD/IRD).  The
# package's own scale test is used so this echo matches what dina_subgroup()
# actually clears.  All three dina-* arms share this floor; they differ only in
# sg_focus / selection_rule / effect_neighborhood.
.dina_identity <- forestsearch:::is_identity_scale(fs_params$effect_measure)
dina_m_diff    <- if (.dina_identity) fs_effect_threshold else log(fs_effect_threshold)
cat(sprintf(
  "DINA harm floor -> m_diff = %.4f  (link scale; %s)\n",
  dina_m_diff,
  if (.dina_identity)
    sprintf("identity = %.4g for %s", fs_effect_threshold, fs_params$effect_measure)
  else
    sprintf("log(%.2f) for %s", fs_effect_threshold, fs_params$effect_measure)))

# -- Derived locals consumed by later chunks ---------------------------------
grf_params <- list(
  dmin.grf     = grf_dmin,
  maxdepth     = grf_maxdepth,
  sg.criterion = grf_sg_criterion
)

# Re-exposed for the single-trial sanity-check chunks.
c1       <- fs_params$hr.threshold
max_look <- fs_params$max_subgroups_search

# Display helper: tidy a cut-string for DISPLAY only (rounds full-precision
# numeric thresholds to `digits` significant figures; collapses whitespace,
# leaves integer cuts untouched).  Used by the subgroup-distribution renders.
tidy_sg_def <- function(s, digits = 4L) {
  if (length(s) != 1L || is.na(s) || !nzchar(s)) return(s)
  s <- gsub("[[:space:]]+", " ", s)
  m <- gregexpr("-?[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+", s)[[1L]]
  if (m[1L] == -1L) return(s)
  L <- attr(m, "match.length")
  for (i in rev(seq_along(m))) {
    num <- as.numeric(substr(s, m[i], m[i] + L[i] - 1L))
    rep <- sub("\\.$", "", formatC(signif(num, digits), format = "fg", flag = "#"))
    s <- paste0(substr(s, 1L, m[i] - 1L), rep, substr(s, m[i] + L[i], nchar(s)))
  }
  s
}

# Document-level timing accumulator; each major chunk populates its slot, and
# the bottom-of-document Timing Summary renders the collated values ("—" if unset).
timings <- list()
```

```{r pareto-prep}
#| include: false

library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(gt)

# Loaded for the validation section; the figure itself is self-contained.
have_fs <- requireNamespace("forestsearch", quietly = TRUE)

EFFECT_NEIGHBORHOOD <- 0.10   # the package default

# Mirror of forestsearch internal .pareto_dominated_xy(): both axes maximized.
dominated_xy <- function(x, y) {
  n <- length(x)
  dom <- logical(n)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    if (is.na(x[i]) || is.na(y[i])) { dom[i] <- TRUE; next }
    for (j in seq_len(n)) {
      if (i == j) next
      if (is.na(x[j]) || is.na(y[j])) next
      if (x[j] >= x[i] && y[j] >= y[i] && (x[j] > x[i] || y[j] > y[i])) {
        dom[i] <- TRUE
        break
      }
    }
  }
  dom
}
```

# Purpose

`forestsearch()` (and, since v0.2.0, `dina_subgroup()`) selects among the
qualifying candidate subgroups using `sg_focus`. For the effect-anchored
foci `"effMaxSG"`/`"effMinSG"` (canonical `"hrMaxSG"`/`"hrMinSG"`), the
selection is *not* "take the candidate with the largest effect." Instead
the candidates are first partitioned into a **candidate inclusion band**,
and then ranked within that band by sample size. The `selection_rule`
argument controls how the band is drawn:

* `"neighborhood"` --- a one-dimensional effect band (default).
* `"pareto"` --- the two-dimensional Pareto-non-dominated set in
  (effect, $N$) space.
* `"both"` --- the intersection of the two (strictest).

This note explains how the **Pareto frontier** operates: what
"dominated" means, how the frontier becomes the `in_pareto` indicator,
how it combines with the neighborhood band, and how the resulting
`in_band` flag feeds the final selection sort. The single computation
shared by every path is `.compute_inclusion_band()`, called by both
`sort_subgroups()` (final, post-consistency selection) and
`sort_subgroups_preview()` (pre-consistency triage).

# A worked candidate set

Five candidates that have already passed the consistency stage and the
effect threshold. Effect on the natural (HR) scale, size $N$:

```{r candidates}
cands <- data.table(
  id = c("A", "B", "C", "E", "F"),
  hr = c(2.50, 2.40, 2.30, 2.35, 2.00),
  N  = c(70L,  100L, 150L, 90L,  200L)
)

hr_max  <- max(cands$hr)
hr_floor <- (1 - EFFECT_NEIGHBORHOOD) * hr_max

cands[, in_nbhd     := hr >= hr_floor]
cands[, dominated   := dominated_xy(hr, N)]
cands[, on_frontier := !dominated]
cands[, in_both     := in_nbhd & on_frontier]
cands[, status      := fifelse(!in_nbhd, "neither (below floor)",
                        fifelse(in_both,  "both rules",
                                          "neighborhood only"))]

# effMaxSG within the "both" band: largest N among in-band-both candidates.
sel_id <- cands[in_both == TRUE][order(-N)][1L, id]
cands[, selected := id == sel_id]

cands[, .(id, hr, N, in_nbhd, on_frontier, in_both, selected)]
```

With `hr_max = 2.5`, the floor is `r round(hr_floor, 3)`. So:

* `A`, `B`, `C` are in the effect band **and** on the frontier --- in-band
  under every rule.
* `E` (HR 2.35, $N$ 90) is in the effect band but **dominated by `B`**
  (HR 2.40 $\ge$ 2.35 and $N$ 100 $\ge$ 90), so `"pareto"`/`"both"`
  exclude it while `"neighborhood"` keeps it.
* `F` (HR 2.00, $N$ 200) is on the frontier (largest $N$) but **below the
  floor**, so `"neighborhood"`/`"both"` exclude it while `"pareto"`
  keeps it --- this is the over-extension guard that the effect band
  provides and the bare frontier does not.

# The figure

```{r}
#| label: fig-frontier
#| fig-width: 7.2
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-cap: "Candidate subgroups in the (effect, N) plane. The shaded region is the effect neighborhood band (HR at least the dashed floor); the dashed line traces the Pareto frontier. Colour encodes which selection_rule keeps each candidate. C is selected by effMaxSG (largest N in the band)."

pal <- c("both rules"           = "#1D9E75",
         "neighborhood only"    = "#EF9F27",
         "neither (below floor)" = "#888780")

frontier <- cands[on_frontier == TRUE][order(hr)]

# per-point label offsets so the letters sit clear of points/lines
labs <- data.table(
  id = c("A", "B", "C", "E", "F"),
  lx = c(2.50, 2.435, 2.30, 2.35, 2.00),
  ly = c(63,   108,   166,  79,   210))

ggplot(cands, aes(hr, N)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = hr_floor, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#378ADD", alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = hr_floor, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "#185FA5", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line(data = frontier, aes(hr, N), linetype = "dashed",
            colour = "#888780", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = cands[selected == TRUE], aes(hr, N),
             shape = 21, size = 9, stroke = 1.3,
             colour = "#0F6E56", fill = NA) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = status), size = 3.6) +
  geom_text(data = labs, aes(lx, ly, label = id),
            size = 4, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = hr_floor + 0.015, y = 219,
           label = sprintf("HR >= %.2f  (within %.0f%% of max)",
                           hr_floor, 100 * EFFECT_NEIGHBORHOOD),
           hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 3.1, colour = "#185FA5") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal, name = "in_band under") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(1.9, 2.62)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(45, 222)) +
  labs(x = "effect (HR)", y = "subgroup size N") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

Reading the figure: `"neighborhood"` keeps the whole shaded strip
$\{A, B, C, E\}$; `"both"` additionally drops `E` because it sits
*inside* the frontier (another point beats it on both axes); `"pareto"`
alone would keep `F` (top-left, on the frontier) despite its weak
effect. The selection then maximizes $N$ within the kept set.


# Data Preparation {#sec-data}

```{r data-prep}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "ACTG175 data prep (click to expand)"

# ACTG175: arm 1 = ZDV+ddI (experimental), arm 3 = ddI (control)
actg_df <- subset(speff2trial::ACTG175, arms %in% c(1L, 3L))
actg_df$id <- seq_len(nrow(actg_df))

# Treatment: ZDV+ddI = 1, ddI = 0 (NO switching)
actg_df$treat <- ifelse(actg_df$arms == 1L, 1L, 0L)

# Binary outcome: adverse (failure to improve)
actg_df$y_binary <- as.integer(actg_df$cd420 <= actg_df$cd40)
actg_df <- actg_df[!is.na(actg_df$cd420), ]

# -- DGM factor variables -----------------------------------------------------
# Note that binary and continuous analyses are similar in identified subgroups
# (from observed-data FS result — see companion analysis document)

 actg_df$z1  <- as.factor(ifelse(actg_df$cd40 > 390, 1L, 0L))
 actg_df$z2  <- as.factor(ifelse(actg_df$wtkg > 80, 1L, 0L))

# z7-z12: truly binary indicators (no continuous counterpart)
actg_df$z7  <- as.factor(actg_df$hemo)
actg_df$z8  <- as.factor(actg_df$homo)
actg_df$z9  <- as.factor(actg_df$drugs)
actg_df$z10 <- as.factor(actg_df$race)
actg_df$z11 <- as.factor(actg_df$gender)
actg_df$z12 <- as.factor(actg_df$symptom)

actg_df$ar_naive   <- as.integer(ifelse(actg_df$str2 == 0, 1L, 0L))
actg_df$prior_6mo  <- as.integer(ifelse(actg_df$preanti <= 6 * 30.4375, 1L, 0L))

actg_df$flag_harm_ref <- as.integer(actg_df$z1 == 1 & actg_df$z2 == 1)

# -- Analysis covariates (what the analyst sees) -------------------------------
cont_vars <- c("age", "preanti", "wtkg", "karnof", "cd40", "cd80")
bin_vars  <- c("hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom","ar_naive","prior_6mo")
# Binary confounders kept NUMERIC 0/1: the forestsearch-routed dina-* arms
# require numeric covariates, and grf-* cut-strings (e.g. "symptom <= 0") must
# be numeric to evaluate.  z7-z12 (created above) stay factors for the DGM.
for (v in bin_vars) actg_df[[v]] <- as.integer(actg_df[[v]])
confounders <- c(cont_vars, bin_vars)


# -- DGM variable sets ---------------------------------------------------------
dgm_factor_vars   <- c("z1", "z2", paste0("z", 7:12))
dgm_cont_vars     <- cont_vars
dgm_subgroup_vars <- c("z1", "z2")
dgm_subgroup_cuts <- list(z1 = 1L, z2 = 1L)

# -- Summary -------------------------------------------------------------------
Q_n   <- sum(actg_df$flag_harm_ref)
Q_N   <- nrow(actg_df)
Q_pct <- 100 * Q_n / Q_N

cat(sprintf("N = %d, Q prevalence = %d / %d (%.1f%%)\n", Q_N, Q_n, Q_N, Q_pct))
cat(sprintf("Adverse rate: overall=%.1f%%, ZDV+ddI=%.1f%%, ddI=%.1f%%\n",
    100 * mean(actg_df$y_binary),
    100 * mean(actg_df$y_binary[actg_df$treat == 1]),
    100 * mean(actg_df$y_binary[actg_df$treat == 0])))
```

# DGM Calibration {#sec-calibration}

Target: OR(Q) = `r cal_target_or` on the adverse scale.  The DGM
includes factor variables (for subgroup definition) and raw continuous
covariates (for a richer prognostic baseline), consistent with the
survival `generate_aft_dgm_flex()` design.

```{r calibrate}
dgm_calibrated <- calibrate_glm_interaction(
  data            = actg_df,
  factor_vars     = dgm_factor_vars,
  continuous_vars = dgm_cont_vars,
  outcome_var     = "y_binary",
  treatment_var   = "treat",
  target_effect   = cal_target_or,
  outcome_type    = "binary",
  effect_measure  = "OR",
  subgroup_vars   = dgm_subgroup_vars,
  subgroup_cuts   = dgm_subgroup_cuts,
  k_inter_range   = c(0, 3),
  grid_step       = 0.05,
  n_super         = 5000L,
  seed            = 8316951L,
  verbose         = TRUE
)

cat(sprintf("\n  OR(Q):   %.3f (target: %.1f)\n",
    dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup, cal_target_or))
cat(sprintf("  OR(Qc):  %.3f\n", dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$no_harm_subgroup))
cat(sprintf("  OR(ITT): %.3f\n", dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$overall))
```

::: {.callout-note title="True harm subgroup Q — definition and calibrated effect"}
**Definition.** The data-generating harm subgroup is
$Q = \{\,\texttt{cd40} > 390 \;\text{and}\; \texttt{wtkg} > 80\,\}$,
encoded by the DGM markers `z1` ($\texttt{cd40} > 390$) and `z2`
($\texttt{wtkg} > 80$); a subject belongs to $Q$ only when **both** hold.

**Prevalence.** `r Q_n` of `r Q_N` subjects (`r sprintf("%.1f", Q_pct)`%) lie in $Q$.

**Calibrated treatment effect** (adverse odds-ratio scale):

- $\operatorname{OR}(Q) =$ `r sprintf("%.3f", dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup)` (target `r sprintf("%.1f", cal_target_or)`)
- $\operatorname{OR}(Q^{c}) =$ `r sprintf("%.3f", dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$no_harm_subgroup)`
- $\operatorname{OR}(\text{ITT}) =$ `r sprintf("%.3f", dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$overall)`

Under the harm orientation, $Q$ is the region where the experimental arm
*raises* the adverse-event odds; $Q^{c}$ and the ITT population are calibrated
to be near-null by construction.
:::

```{r null-dgm}
dgm_null <- generate_glm_dgm(
  data            = actg_df,
  factor_vars     = dgm_factor_vars,
  continuous_vars = dgm_cont_vars,
  outcome_var     = "y_binary",
  treatment_var   = "treat",
  outcome_type    = "binary",
  subgroup_vars   = dgm_subgroup_vars,
  subgroup_cuts   = dgm_subgroup_cuts,
  model           = "null",
  n_super         = 5000L,
  seed            = 8316951L,
  verbose         = TRUE
)
```

# Single Trial Sanity Check {#sec-single-trial}

```{r single-trial-alt-sim}
#| eval: !expr run_single_trial
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Single simulated trial + FS analysis alt (click to expand)"
df_sim <- simulate_from_glm_dgm(dgm_calibrated, n = sim_n, seed = 42)
```


```{r single-trial-alt-analysis}
#| eval: !expr run_single_trial
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Single simulated trial + FS analysis alt (click to expand)"

itt_fit <- glm(y_sim ~ treat_sim, family = "binomial", data = df_sim)
itt_OR <- exp(coef(itt_fit)["treat_sim"])
itt_event <- with(df_sim,mean(y_sim))

fs_params_single <- fs_params

fs_params_single$show_candidate_summary <- TRUE 
fs_params_single$parallel_args$plan <- "multisession"
fs_params_single$parallel_args$workers <- n_workers

fs_single <- do.call(forestsearch, c(
  list(df.analysis = df_sim, confounders.name = confounders),
  fs_params_single
))

if (!is.null(fs_single$sg.harm)) {
  fs_single_tabs <- sg_tables(fs_single, ndecimals = 3)
}

t0 <- proc.time()
fs <- fs_single

if (!is.null(fs$sg.harm)) {
  fs_bc <- forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(
    fs.est = fs,
    nb_boots = 500,
    show_three = FALSE,
    details = FALSE,
    parallel_args = list(
      plan = "multisession",
      workers = n_workers,
      show_message = TRUE
    )
  )

  plan("sequential")
  timings$bootstrap_alt <- as.numeric((proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"])

  cat("\nBootstrap completed in",
      round(timings$bootstrap_alt / 60, 1), "minutes\n")

  # Comprehensive summary with diagnostics.  All variables built here are
  # rendered by the small downstream chunks (single-trial-alt-render-*),
  # which exist solely so each gt table is the last (and only) expression
  # of its chunk -- the only way knitr's auto-print reliably emits raw
  # HTML for a gt_tbl object.
  summaries <- summarize_bootstrap_results(
    sgharm = fs$sg.harm,
    boot_results = fs_bc,
    create_plots = TRUE,
    est.scale = "hr"
  )

  ci_tab <- compute_frontier_cis(
    fs,
    n_splits = frontier_params$n_splits,
    seed     = frontier_params$seed
  )

  # Plot rendered inline here -- the graphics-device path is independent
  # of knitr's stdout capture, so print(p) works inside the if-block.
  p <- plot_pareto_frontier(
    fs,
    ci_table  = ci_tab,
    show_band = TRUE,
    xlim      = frontier_params$xlim
  )
  print(p)
}
```

```{r fs-loo-setup}
#| eval: !expr run_single_trial
# Define run_loo BEFORE the LOO run chunk so its #| eval: directive can
# reference it.  Chunk options are evaluated before the chunk body, so
# run_loo must already exist in the global env when knitr resolves the
# next chunk's options.
#
# skip_loo is the explicit negation -- defined here so the downstream
# "LOO skipped" note can gate on a plain identifier rather than the
# expression !run_loo, which trips Quarto's YAML validator
# (it parses `!expr !run_loo` as a string, not the expected tagged form).
run_loo   <- !is.null(fs$sg.harm)
skip_loo  <- !run_loo
```

```{r fs-loo-run}
#| eval: !expr run_single_trial && run_loo

t0 <- proc.time()

# LOO is triggered by Kfolds = N (the function default behavior at
# forestsearch_cross_validation.R:109).  We pass it explicitly here for
# clarity.
N_loo <- nrow(fs$df.est)

fs_loo_result <- forestsearch_Kfold(
  fs.est        = fs,
  Kfolds        = N_loo,
  seedit        = analysis_seed,
  parallel_args = list(
    plan = "multisession",
    workers = n_workers,
    show_message = TRUE
  ),
  details       = FALSE
)

plan("sequential"); gc(verbose = FALSE)
timings$loo_alt <- as.numeric((proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"])

cat("\nLOO completed in", round(timings$loo_alt / 60, 2), "minutes",
    sprintf("(N folds = %d, n_workers = %d)\n", N_loo, n_workers))
```

### LOO Tables

The `cv_summary_tables()` helper returns five publication-ready `gt`
tables. The first is the combined ITT + subgroup view; the next three
are component estimation tables (ITT, full-analysis subgroup, LOO
subgroup) that show the underlying treatment-effect estimates with
confidence intervals.

```{r fs-loo-tables}

                                  digits = 2)
loo_tabs <- cv_summary_tables(
  loo_out,
  title    = "ACTG175 Leave-One-Out CV Summary (Binary, OR)",
  subtitle = sprintf("ITT and Subgroup Estimates: Full Analysis (FA) vs LOO (N=%d)",
                     N_loo),
  digits   = 2,
  use_gt   = TRUE
)
```

```{r single-trial-null-analysis}
    create_plots = TRUE,
    est.scale = "hr"
  )
  
  ci_tab <- compute_frontier_cis(
    fs,
    n_splits = frontier_params$n_splits,
    seed     = frontier_params$seed
  )
  
  # Plot rendered inline here -- the graphics-device path is independent
  # of knitr's stdout capture, so print(p) works inside the if-block.
  p <- plot_pareto_frontier(
    fs,
    ci_table  = ci_tab,
    show_band = TRUE,
    xlim      = frontier_params$xlim
  )
  print(p)
}
```

```{r fs-loo-setup-null}
#| eval: !expr run_single_trial
# Define run_loo BEFORE the LOO run chunk so its #| eval: directive can
# reference it.  Chunk options are evaluated before the chunk body, so
# run_loo must already exist in the global env when knitr resolves the
# next chunk's options.
#
# skip_loo is the explicit negation -- defined here so the downstream
# "LOO skipped" note can gate on a plain identifier rather than the
# expression !run_loo, which trips Quarto's YAML validator
# (it parses `!expr !run_loo` as a string, not the expected tagged form).
run_loo   <- !is.null(fs$sg.harm)
skip_loo  <- !run_loo
```

```{r fs-loo-run-null}
#| eval: !expr run_single_trial && run_loo

t0 <- proc.time()

# LOO is triggered by Kfolds = N (the function default behavior at
# forestsearch_cross_validation.R:109).  We pass it explicitly here for
# clarity.
N_loo <- nrow(fs$df.est)

fs_loo_result <- forestsearch_Kfold(
  fs.est        = fs,
  Kfolds        = N_loo,
  seedit        = analysis_seed,
  parallel_args = list(
    plan = "multisession",
    workers = n_workers,
    show_message = TRUE
  ),
  details       = FALSE
)

plan("sequential"); gc(verbose = FALSE)
timings$loo_null <- as.numeric((proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"])

cat("\nLOO completed in", round(timings$loo_null / 60, 2), "minutes",
    sprintf("(N folds = %d, n_workers = %d)\n", N_loo, n_workers))
```

## Mode Handoff

```{r mode-handoff}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Bundle import or sim-result handoff (click to expand)"

if (sim_mode == "import") {
  bundle <- readRDS(BUNDLE_PATH)

  # Override the freshly-built DGMs with the bundle's versions so that
  # downstream OC tables match the simulation results they describe.
  dgm_calibrated <- bundle$dgm$calibrated
  dgm_null       <- bundle$dgm$null

  results_alt    <- bundle$results$alt
  results_null   <- bundle$results$null
  t_alt          <- bundle$meta$t_alt_sec
  t_null         <- bundle$meta$t_null_sec
  nsims_alt      <- bundle$meta$n_alt
  nsims_null     <- bundle$meta$n_null
  n_failed_alt   <- bundle$meta$n_failed_alt
  n_failed_null  <- bundle$meta$n_failed_null

  cat(sprintf("Imported bundle: %s\n", BUNDLE_PATH))
  cat(sprintf("  config_id : %s\n", bundle$meta$config_id))
  cat(sprintf("  timestamp : %s\n", format(bundle$meta$timestamp)))
  cat(sprintf("  n_alt     : %d (failed: %d)\n",
              nsims_alt, n_failed_alt))
  cat(sprintf("  n_null    : %d (failed: %d)\n",
              nsims_null, n_failed_null))
  if (!is.null(bundle$meta$package_version)) {
    cat(sprintf("  forestsearch %s\n", bundle$meta$package_version))
  }
  if (!is.null(bundle$meta$config_id) &&
      bundle$meta$config_id != CONFIG_ID) {
    warning(sprintf(
      "Bundle config_id ('%s') does not match this article ('%s').",
      bundle$meta$config_id, CONFIG_ID
    ), call. = FALSE)
  }
} else {
  cat(sprintf("Inline simulation complete (%s mode).\n", sim_mode))
}
```

# Results {#sec-results}

## Metrics Glossary {#sec-glossary}

Classification metrics follow the definitions in León et al.
(2024, Section 3).

### Detection

**Found** ($\text{any}(Q)$): proportion of simulations where
the method identifies *any* harm subgroup
($\texttt{any.H} = 1$).

- **Under H1** (alternative): $Q$ exists with a differential
  treatment effect.  $\text{any}(Q)$ is **detection power**.
- **Under H0** (null): $Q = \emptyset$ and $Q^c$ is the ITT
  population.  $\text{any}(Q)$ is the **false positive rate
  (FPR)** for falsely declaring that a harm subgroup exists.

### Classification Under H1

Under the alternative, the true harm subgroup $Q$ exists
($Q = \{\text{cd40} > 421 \cap \text{wtkg} > 82.3\}$,
prevalence $\approx$ `r sprintf("%.0f", Q_pct)`%)
with a genuinely different treatment effect (OR(Q) =
`r cal_target_or`).  Following León et al. (2024, Section 3),
define for estimated subgroup $\hat{Q}$:

$$
\text{sens}(\hat{Q}) = \frac{\#\{i \in \hat{Q} \cap Q\}}{\#\{i \in Q\}},
\quad
\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}) = \frac{\#\{i \in \hat{Q} \cap Q\}}{\#\{i \in \hat{Q}\}},
$$

with analogous measures for the complement $\hat{Q}^c$.

The operating-characteristics tables report these as:

| Table column | León et al. notation | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| **Sen** | $\text{sens}(\hat{Q})$ | Fraction of true $Q$ captured by $\hat{Q}$ |
| **Spec** | $\text{sens}(\hat{Q}^c)$ | Fraction of true $Q^c$ correctly in $\hat{Q}^c$ |
| **PPV** | $\text{ppv}(\hat{Q})$ | Fraction of $\hat{Q}$ truly in $Q$ |
| **NPV** | $\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}^c)$ | Fraction of $\hat{Q}^c$ truly in $Q^c$ |

Classification metrics are averaged across **all** simulations
(León et al. 2024, Table 1).  When no subgroup is detected
($\hat{Q} = \emptyset$), the simulation contributes
$\text{sens}(\hat{Q}) = 0$ and $\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}) = 0$
(since no member of $Q$ is captured and no subjects are
assigned to $\hat{Q}$).  This convention is implemented
at the source in `run_simulation_analysis()`, matching
the original `fs.estimates.out()` function used in
León et al. (2024).

::: {.callout-note}
## Classification metrics with discovered cuts

Because cuts are discovered from the data in this setup, a
$\hat{Q}$ that captures "roughly the right region" but with
slightly shifted boundaries will still receive high sens/PPV.
Expect these metrics to be lower than under the discretised
(oracle-cut) setup — the gap quantifies the cost of not knowing
the true cuts in advance.
:::

### Classification Under H0

Under the null, $Q = \emptyset$ --- no subgroup with a
differential treatment effect exists.  The complement $Q^c$
is the entire ITT population.  Per León et al. (2024,
Section 3), $\text{sens}(\hat{Q})$ is **undefined** (shown
as "—" in the table) and $\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}) \equiv 0$.
For the complement, $\text{sens}(\hat{Q}^c) = |\hat{Q}^c|/N$
and $\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}^c) = 1$ since $Q^c$ = ITT.

The only operationally meaningful metric under H0 is the
**detection rate (FPR)**.

### Effect Estimates

All effect estimates are on the adverse scale:
OR $> 1$ = treatment (ZDV+ddI) increases the adverse outcome
(non-improvement) = **harm**.  No inversion or treatment
switching is applied.

# Operating Characteristics {#sec-oc}

## H1: Detection + Classification

```{r oc-alt}
format_oc_results(
  results_alt,
  metrics   = c("detection", "classification", "subgroup_size"),
  digits    = 2,
  digits_hr = 2,
  title     = "ACTG175 Binary: Harm Subgroup Identification",
  dgm = dgm_calibrated,
  subgroup_notation = sg_notation
)
```

### True Subgroup Sizes Across Replicates

```{r true-size-summary}
#| code-fold: true

# One row per replicate-method combination, but sizeH_true is identical
# across method rows within the same sim.  Deduplicate on sim.
truth_by_sim <- unique(results_alt[, c("sim", "sizeH_true", "sizeHc_true",
                                        "propH_true", "propHc_true")])

callout_Q <- sprintf(
  "|Q|:  mean = %.1f (SD %.2f),  range = [%d, %d],  prop = %.1f%%",
  mean(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true),
  sd(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true),
  min(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true),
  max(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true),
  100 * mean(truth_by_sim$propH_true))

callout_Qc <- sprintf(
  "|Qc|: mean = %.1f (SD %.2f),  range = [%d, %d],  prop = %.1f%%",
  mean(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true),
  sd(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true),
  min(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true),
  max(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true),
  100 * mean(truth_by_sim$propHc_true))

cat(sprintf("True subgroup sizes across %d H1 replicates (N = %d each):\n",
            nrow(truth_by_sim), sim_n))
cat("  ", callout_Q,  "\n")
cat("  ", callout_Qc, "\n")
```

::: {.callout-note title="Reference sizes for the estimation tables below"}
- **|Q| (true harm subgroup)**: mean `r sprintf("%.1f", mean(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true))`
  per trial (SD `r sprintf("%.2f", sd(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true))`,
  range `r min(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true)`–`r max(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true)`,
  average proportion `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(truth_by_sim$propH_true))`).
- **|Qc| (complement)**: mean `r sprintf("%.1f", mean(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true))`
  per trial (SD `r sprintf("%.2f", sd(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true))`,
  range `r min(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true)`–`r max(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true)`,
  average proportion `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(truth_by_sim$propHc_true))`).

Compare to $\widehat{|H|}$ (the FS-identified subgroup size) reported in
the row-group labels of the estimation tables below.  A ratio
$\widehat{|H|} \big/ \overline{|Q|} \approx 1$ indicates the method is
recovering a subgroup close to the true size; values much smaller
suggest FS is identifying a strict subset of $Q$; values larger suggest
FS is absorbing some $Q^c$ subjects into $\hat H$.
:::
